raw_response:
I've been farming these 22.1 mu for many years, so I know what works here. Let me think it through.

I have cotton, maize, stevia, and wheat to manage. I don't plant them all at once — wheat goes in autumn and comes off in June, then maize goes on the same ground. Cotton I plant in April on its own land. Stevia stays on its own plot too because it's more trouble and needs more water.

I split the land like this: cotton on 8 mu (that's my main crop, the system here), wheat and maize double-cropped on 10 mu (that's our normal way — save the land, two harvests), and stevia on 4.1 mu. Stevia the company buys from us so I keep some.

For fertilizer I buy 复合肥 (compound, 15-15-15) at the dealer in town, then add urea (尿素) when the crop is growing. My neighbor Wang uses about 2 bags of compound per mu for wheat plus 1 bag urea for topdressing — I do the same, maybe a little more urea because last year my wheat looked yellow in March. Better to give too much than lose the harvest.

Cotton eats a lot of potash or the bolls don't fill. I put extra 钾肥 on cotton. Cotton also needs many pesticide sprays — bollworm, aphids, red spider. I spray maybe 6-7 times, that's normal here.

Stevia I water more because the leaves need to be thick. The company tells us how to manage it but I mostly do what I've always done plus what they say about harvest timing.

Wheat I plough before planting. Maize after wheat I just rotary — no time to plough, must plant fast. Cotton I plough deep in spring.

I use improved seed for all — the dealer sells good varieties, my neighbors use the same.
